title: Provider Credentialing and Practice Lead
description: Mission Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear. In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives. Role Purpose The Clinical Practicec Lead owns practice management for Neko Health's United States professional corporation. The role covers four areas: provider credentialing, SOP organization and maintenance, onboarding operationalization, and compliance assurance. Neko runs a tech-enabled clinical model, and this role is expected to run all four through systems and automation rather than manual tracking. Credentialing: the role holds the credential file for every provider practicing under the PC: license, certification, permitted scope by state, malpractice coverage details and every other expirable, verified at source and kept current so that no provider ever sees a member on a lapsed credential. While Neko does not credential with payers today - this role runs the credentialing gate that clears a provider to practice and removes that clearance when a credential lapses. It supplies provider credentialing data into the clinic compliance systems and works to the credentialing standard and clear-to-practice definition set by the Head of Compliance. SOPs: the role owns the SOP library for US practice operations. The role keeps every SOP current, versioned, and easy to find, and retires SOPs that no longer apply. Onboarding: the role turns each new provider's onboarding plan into a working, tracked sequence: credentialing, system access, training, and clearance to start, in the right order and against a clear timeline. Compliance: the role checks that US practice operations meet the standards set by the Head of Compliance, and reports gaps as they surface. Systems and automation: the role chooses, configures and owns the tooling that carries all of the above — one source of truth for provider data, automated expiry alerts, and workflows that hand off cleanly between Talent Acquisition, the People Team, IT and clinical operations. Status should be visible from the system rather than assembled by hand. As Neko opens further states, credentialing volume and complexity grow faster than headcount, and practice operations grow with them. This role exists to make provider readiness, SOP currency, onboarding execution, and compliance standing a managed process with evidence behind it, built on tooling that scales faster than headcount, rather than a scramble before each launch. What You'll Deliver in the First 6–12 Months A current, auditable register of every clinician's license, credential, and permitted scope by state, held in a single system of record with automated expiry tracking and a named process for renewal before lapse. A complete credential file per provider practicing under the PC, with primary source verification evidence attached and dated. A written credentialing procedure covering intake, verification, the clear-to-practice decision, re-verification cycle, and removal of clearance. The credentialing gate built into the clinician onboarding sequence, so a start date cannot be confirmed without verified credentials. A current SOP library for US practice operations: indexed, version-controlled, and reviewed on a set cycle. An onboarding operations sequence that turns each new provider's plan into a tracked timeline from offer to start, with the credentialing gate built in. Practice operations running in-system rather than on spreadsheets: onboarding, SOP review cycles and compliance checks tracked in Neko's tooling, with the remaining manual steps documented and a plan to remove them. A compliance status report showing where US practice operations meet the Head of Compliance's standards, and where they do not, generated from the system rather than compiled by hand. Key Responsibilities Provider credentialing and primary source verification Run credentialing intake for every new provider joining the PC: application, document collection, and verification at source rather than from candidate-supplied copies. Verify state medical/nursing licenses, board certification, education and training, work history, and DEA registration where the provider's scope requires it. Operate the clear-to-practice gate: no provider is released to see members until the credential file is complete and verified. Maintain the permitted scope by state for each provider and flag to the Head of Compliance any request to practice outside it. Expirables, re-verification and removal Own the expirables calendar for licenses, certifications, DEA registrations, malpractice coverage and any other time-limited credential, driven by automated alerts rather than manual review. Chase renewals ahead of expiry against defined lead times and escalate when a renewal is at risk. Remove clearance to practice immediately when a credential lapses and notify the clinical rota owner and the Head of Compliance the same day. Run the re-verification cycle so credential files do not silently age. Systems, tooling and automation Select, implement and administer the tooling that runs practice operations: credentialing records, expiry tracking, onboarding workflow and SOP version control. Replace manual tracking with automated alerts, scheduled reporting and system-driven handoffs, and keep a running list of the steps still done by hand. Define the data structure behind credentialing and onboarding so status can be reported out of the system rather than reconstructed. Work with IT and, where relevant, product and engineering to integrate practice operations data with adjacent systems instead of maintaining parallel spreadsheets. SOP organization and maintenance Own the SOP library for US practice operations: create, index, and version every procedure. Review each SOP on a set cycle and update it when a process changes. Retire SOPs that no longer apply, and flag processes that run without one. Keep SOPs easy to find and use for the staff who rely on them day to day. Onboarding operationalization Turn each new provider's onboarding plan into a tracked sequence: credentialing, system access, training, and clearance to start. Own the onboarding timeline from offer to start date, and flag delays before they hit the start date. Coordinate with Talent Acquisition, the People Team, and clinical operations to keep the sequence moving. Improve the onboarding sequence as volume grows, including automation of tracking and reminders. Compliance assurance Confirm that US practice operations meet the standards set by the Head of Compliance. Run periodic checks against those standards, and report gaps as they surface. Support audits of practice operations with evidence drawn from SOPs, onboarding records, and the credentialing file. Escalate compliance gaps that need action beyond this role. Credentialing process, data and reporting Keep the credentialing record system accurate and audit-ready, so a credential file can be produced on request without reconstruction. Report credentialing status, upcoming expiries and blocked providers into the Medical Quality reporting cycle, on a set cadence and drawn from the system of record. Improve the credentialing process as volume grows, including automation of tracking and reminders. Prepare the function for payer credentialing and provider enrollment should Neko US move to billing insurance. About you Minimum Requirements Experience streamlining clinical or healthcare operations in a tech-enabled environment: you have taken a manual, spreadsheet-run process and rebuilt it as a system-driven workflow, and you can describe what you removed and what changed as a result. Experience working in a clinical operations capacity – where you were responsible for not just executing but building the systems to ensure credentialing, compliance and other clinical operations processes are handled excellently. Confident with operational tooling: you configure and administer the systems you depend on rather than raising a ticket for every change, and you are comfortable working with data, reporting and everyday automation. Direct, hands-on experience of state medical board licensure and clinician credentialing processes, including primary source verification. Experience maintaining a credentialing database or record system to an audit-ready standard. Experience developing, organizing, and maintaining SOPs in a clinical or regulated operations setting. Working knowledge of compliance standards in a healthcare or clinical operations setting, with experience checking operations against them. Precise and persistent administratively Preferred Experience in a digital health, telehealth or otherwise tech-enabled care setting, where clinical operations run on product and tooling rather than paper. Hands-on experience with credentialing or provider data platforms, and with the workflow and tracking tools used to run operations day to day. Experience working alongside product or engineering teams to specify what operational tooling needs to do. Direct experience provider credentialing in a United States clinical setting, including multi-state credentialing. Experience of credentialing in a newly opened market or a start-up clinical service where the process did not yet exist. Experience building an SOP program from scratch in a growing or newly opened operation. Everything is moving faster than ever before. AI progress is only accelerating. Startups are achieving growth goals in months that used to take years. Whole industries are being obliterated overnight.

As an ex-founder, change is your second nature. You know how to adapt, to grow beyond yourself to meet the challenge.
You have been in the trenches for years. You have a sixth sense about the things that matter amidst chaos, an intuition that is almost impossible to learn.

Small teams of excellent people can punch way above their weight and achieve things that seemed impossible months ago.

We are assembling a team of kick-ass former founders to do our life’s best work together.

Our ambition is to invent the future of work. We will beat Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI, and Google on the application layer.
We developed the platform that allows companies to rethink their processes fundamentally and make them agentic.

In other words, we are building the token value machine that allows enterprises to build agentic systems that generate more ROI the more tokens they invest.

We are hiring ex-founders with a track record in all roles. Engineering, Growth, Product, Deployments.

Let’s talk and see how you fit in.

raw.title: Project Manager - Software Implementation (m/f/x)
raw.description:
Job Title: Project Manager - Software Implementation (m/f/x) 

Location: EU

(Remote) 

 

Who You’ll Work For: 

 

At Makersite, we're pioneering the future of sustainable product development and digital collaboration. As a leading platform for product lifecycle management (PLM), we empower companies to make smarter, more sustainable decisions across their entire supply chain. Our cutting-edge software enables teams to design, prototype, and manufacture with transparency, efficiency, and responsibility—reducing environmental impact while optimizing performance. 

We're a fast-growing, innovative company that thrives on creativity, collaboration, and continuous learning. If you're passionate about technology, sustainability, and creating meaningful impact, we’d love to hear from you. Join us and be a part of shaping the future of manufacturing and product innovation. 

 

Who we're looking for: 

 

As part of our growing team, you will play a key role in shaping the future of sustainable product development. We’re looking for innovative, driven Project Managers who are passionate about technology and sustainability to join us in building tools that enable companies to make smarter, more responsible decisions. In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to collaborate with talented professionals, contribute to cutting-edge projects, and help drive the digital transformation of industries worldwide. If you're ready to make an impact and contribute to meaningful change, we want to hear from you! 

This role is a fixed, permanent position. All successful applicants will receive a permanent employment contract regardless of location.  

 

The role:

  

  • Lead the planning and implementation of software projects related to system connections with our customers, ensuring they are delivered on time and within scope. 

  • Maintain and update project plans, proactively identifying and managing any project risks. 

  • Ensure the availability of the right expertise for each project phase, coordinating with internal and external resources as necessary. 

  • Manage stakeholder expectations, delivering regular and comprehensive project updates and effectively resolving any arising issues. 

  • Contribute to the standardization of project implementation methodology and project templates to improve project standardization and efficiency. 

  • Generate thorough Project/Solution Documentation, outlining project goals, deliverables, and timelines. 

  • Handle all customer communication across various projects, ensuring clear, consistent, and timely communication with all stakeholders. 


  • Master's degree in project management or related technical field required. 

  • Background in Electronics/Electricals

  • Professional Project Management Certification from an accredited institution preferred. 

  • Demonstrated understanding of Project Management processes, strategies, and methods 

  • Excellent time management and organizational skills and experience establishing guidelines in these areas for others. 

  • 3+ years of Project management experience in the field of software implementations 

  • Experience with complex data projects where a systematic approach is crucial to success. 

  • Dexterity with software tools and data manipulation & analysis 

  • A creative mind that can think outside the box. 

  • Curiosity to find disruptive as opposed to incremental solutions to challenging data problems. 

  • Residing in and legally permitted to work in the EU. 

 

What We Offer: 

 

  • Competitive Salary – We reward your skills and experience with a compensation package that reflects your value. 

  • 30 Days Paid Time Off – Take the time you need to recharge and maintain a healthy work-life balance. 

  • Remote-First Flexibility – Work from anywhere in the EU, with the option to collaborate in person at our offices in Stuttgart, Berlin (role dependent). 

  • Generous Learning & Development Budget – We invest in your growth, providing ample resources for personal and professional development. 

  • Choose Your Ideal Work Equipment – Whether you prefer Apple or Microsoft, we’ll equip you with the tools you need to excel. 

 

The Experience: 

 

  • Purpose-Driven Work – Build something meaningful. Here, you’re not just creating another app; you’re contributing to a transformative vision that you can be proud of. 

  • Great Colleagues – Join a team that’s open, transparent, and international. We value inclusivity and foster a culture of collaboration and mutual respect. 

  • Work-Life Balance – As a remote-first company, we trust you to do your best work, your way. You have the flexibility to work when it suits you, ensuring a healthy balance between personal and professional life. 

  • Pride in Impact – We're already making a significant difference with global, well-known customers who share our vision. Be part of something that matters. 

  • Stability with Ambition – With realistic growth plans, we’re committed to changing the way things are made—without sacrificing our ambitious goals for innovation and impact. 

If you want to find out more about what it’s like to work at Makersite, check out our Careers Page here 

  

Diversity and Inclusion 

If you have a medical condition or an individual need for an adjustment to our process, and you believe this may affect your ability to be at your best – please let us know so we can talk about how we can best support you and make any adjustments that may be needed.  

 

At Makersite, we are dedicated to fostering an environment that champions diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging. We believe that diverse teams drive innovation and success, and we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and will consider all applications regardless of age, disability, gender identity, marital status, pregnancy or maternity, race, nationality, religion, sex, sexual orientation, or any other status protected by applicable law. Rest assured, all applications will be handled with the utmost confidentiality.

raw.title: 🍕 Senior Category Manager (m/w/d)
raw.description:
Du möchtest ein umfangreiches FMCG Sortiment nicht nur verwalten, sondern dessen wirtschaftliche Entwicklung aktiv steuern? Du analysierst Performance Daten, triffst fundierte Sortimentsentscheidungen und erkennst, welche Lieferantenbeziehungen besonderes Wachstumspotenzial bieten? 

Dann könnte diese Position genau das Richtige für dich sein. 

Unser Kunde, eine dynamisch wachsende E-Commerce Service Agentur in Berlin, zählt zu den erfolgreichsten Amazon-Händlern Deutschlands und vertreibt tausende Produkte. 
Für die weitere Entwicklung der FMCG Kategorien wird ein Senior Category Manager gesucht, der die kommerzielle Verantwortung für ein breites Sortiment übernimmt und wichtige Lieferantenbeziehungen gezielt weiterentwickelt. 

Deine Benefits

  • Attraktive Vergütung: Ein leistungsgerechtes Fixgehalt, das deiner Erfahrung und Qualifikation entspricht.  

  • Flexibles Arbeiten: Hybrides Arbeitsmodell mit 2 Home-Office Tagen, einer 40-Stunden-Woche, Gleitzeit mit Arbeitsbeginn zwischen 6:00 und 10:00 Uhr.      

  • Langfristige Sicherheit: Unbefristeter Arbeitsvertrag sowie 30 Urlaubstage in einem wirtschaftlich erfolgreichen und zukunftssicheren Unternehmen.  

  • Weiterentwicklung: Ob fachlich oder persönlich – deine Entwicklung wird aktiv gefördert und langfristig begleitet.  

  • Modernes Arbeitsumfeld: Freue dich auf ein modernes Büro im Berliner Bezirk Lichtenberg.  

  • Mobilität: Ob mit den öffentlichen Verkehrsmitteln oder dem Auto – profitiere von einem bezuschussten Jobticket oder kostenlosen Parkplätzen direkt am Büro.  

  • Teamkultur: Flache Hierarchien, offene Kommunikation, eine gelebte Du-Kultur und regelmäßige Team- sowie Firmenevents wie „Grill & Chill“ sorgen für ein starkes Miteinander.  

  • Verpflegung: Kostenlose Getränke sowie frisches Obst stehen dir im Arbeitsalltag jederzeit zur Verfügung.  

  • Mitarbeitervorteile: Profitiere von attraktiven Mitarbeiterrabatten auf das Sortiment sowie weiteren Corporate Benefits. 

Deine Aufgaben

Als Senior Category Manager FMCG übernimmst du die kommerzielle Verantwortung für ein breites Produktsortiment. Du steuerst dessen wirtschaftliche Entwicklung datenbasiert, erkennst Chancen und Risiken frühzeitig und sorgst dafür, dass aus deinen Erkenntnissen konkrete Maßnahmen entstehen. 

  • Kommerzielle Sortimentssteuerung: Verantwortung für Umsatz, Profitabilität, Bestand und Verfügbarkeit der Kategorien und des komplexen Sortiments. 

  • Performanceanalyse: Analyse relevanter Kennzahlen (Umsatz, Marge, Preise, Nachfrage, Wettbewerb, Bestände) und Ableitung konkreter Maßnahmen & Handlungsempfehlungen  

  • Datenbasierte Entscheidungen: Eigenständig Analysen & Auswertungen sowie gezielte Einbindung dess BI Team 

  • Sortimentsentwicklung: Entscheidung über Ausbau, Optimierung, Aufnahme und Auslistung von Artikeln anhand wirtschaftlicher Potenziale. 

  • Lieferantenentwicklung: Identifikation und Ausbau strategisch relevanter Partnerschaften im Lieferantenportfolio 

  • Wachstumsinitiativen: Entwicklung besserer Konditionen, neuer Sortimentspotenziale und gemeinsamer Vermarktungsansätze mit ausgewählten Partnern  

  • Verhandlungen: Datenbasierte Vorbereitung und Führung kommerzieller Lieferantengespräche 

  • Operative Steuerung: Schnelle Reaktion auf Veränderungen bei Preisen, Beständen, Nachfrage und Wettbewerb 

  • Schnittstellenmanagement:  Koordination mit Marketing, Operations, Logistik und BI, sowie Vorantreiben von Entscheidungen und konsequenter Umsetzung.

Dein Profil als Category Manager FMCG

  • Min. 5 Jahre Berufserfahrung im Category Management, Einkauf, Commercial Management oder Sortimentsmanagement, idealerweise im FMCG Bereich oder E Commerce 

  • Erfahrung in der strukturierten Steuerung großer und komplexer Sortimente 

  • Ausgeprägte analytische Kompetenz sowie Erfahrung in der eigenständigen Auswertung umfangreicher Produkt und Performance Daten 

  • Sehr gutes wirtschaftliches Verständnis für die Zusammenhänge zwischen Umsatz, Marge, Konditionen, Bestand, Verfügbarkeit und Wachstum 

  • Erfahrung in der Zusammenarbeit und Verhandlung mit Lieferanten, Herstellern oder externen Geschäftspartnern 

  • Fähigkeit, strategisch relevante Lieferantenbeziehungen zu erkennen und gezielt weiterzuentwickeln 

  • Sicheres Priorisieren mehrerer Themen sowie fundierte Entscheidungen auch unter Zeitdruck 

  • Eigenverantwortliche, pragmatische und lösungsorientierte Arbeitsweise mit ausgeprägtem unternehmerischem Denken 

  • Fließende Deutschkenntnisse und gute Englischkenntnisse 

Die Rolle als Senior Category Manager klingt genau nach dir? Dann schick uns deinen Lebenslauf und wir geben dir in einem kurzen Telefonat alle weiteren Infos zu Stelle und Unternehmen.

title: Senior Software Engineer - Data Search (remote, Europe)
description: Hey, I'm Adrian . I’m hiring a Senior Software Engineer to join the Data Search team at Modash. Modash helps brands find, understand, and work with creators across Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. More than 2,700 companies—including Stanley 1913, Sennheiser, and NordVPN—use us to manage and scale their creator partnerships. Behind that product is a fascinating search problem: helping customers find the right people across 400M+ creator profiles and billions of media files. We’re combining large-scale data processing, traditional retrieval, vector search, multimodal embeddings, and LLMs to make that possible. That’s where you come in. Why we're hiring Search at Modash isn't an internal platform or a support function. It is one of the core products customers use to discover creators. The scale is large, the data is messy, and the search intent is often complex. A customer might be looking for creators in a specific niche, people whose content conveys a certain visual style, or accounts that resemble a group they already know. Solving that well requires more than adding another filter or calling an LLM API. We need a senior engineer who can work across the full retrieval system—from data and indexing pipelines to embeddings, ranking, relevance, and low-latency serving—and take ambiguous product problems all the way to production. You’ll join the specialised Data Search team and work closely with Data Core, Data Insights, product teams, customers, and company leadership. You’ll have real autonomy, but you won’t work in isolation. If you want a feel for how we think about building software, check our Engineering Blog . What you'll actually own 1. Make creator search meaningfully better. You’ll improve how customers discover creators across 400M+ profiles and billions of media files. That includes retrieval, filtering, ranking, relevance, speed, and the product decisions that connect them. 2. Turn multimodal data into searchable intelligence. You’ll build systems that generate and use embeddings from images, video, text, and audio at massive scale—then make those signals useful in a real customer-facing search experience. 3. Ship new search capabilities into production. You’ll evaluate models and technologies pragmatically, understand tradeoffs around cost, latency, and quality, and move promising approaches from experiment to a reliable production system within weeks rather than quarters. 4. Own the system end to end. You’ll help shape the problem, gather requirements, design the architecture, write the code, release it, measure the outcome, and improve it. Senior engineers here own results, not just implementation tasks. What the day-to-day looks like Here’s what a typical week might include: Monday. A customer search is returning technically relevant but unhelpful results. You inspect the retrieval and ranking stages, identify where intent is being lost, and propose a measurable improvement. Tuesday. Deep-focus time. You build a pipeline to generate multimodal embeddings across a large batch of creator content and test how the new representation affects retrieval quality and cost. Wednesday. You work with Data Insights on a new in-house datapoint. Together, you agree on its definition, coverage, and data-quality requirements, then expose it in Search to give customers more ways to discover creators. Thursday. Hey, I'm Adrian. I’m hiring a Senior Software Engineer to join the Data Search team at Modash.

Modash helps brands find, understand, and work with creators across Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. More than 2,700 companies—including Stanley 1913, Sennheiser, and NordVPN—use us to manage and scale their creator partnerships.

Behind that product is a fascinating search problem: helping customers find the right people across 400M+ creator profiles and billions of media files. We’re combining large-scale data processing, traditional retrieval, vector search, multimodal embeddings, and LLMs to make that possible.

That’s where you come in.

Why we're hiring

Search at Modash isn't an internal platform or a support function. It is one of the core products customers use to discover creators.

The scale is large, the data is messy, and the search intent is often complex. A customer might be looking for creators in a specific niche, people whose content conveys a certain visual style, or accounts that resemble a group they already know. Solving that well requires more than adding another filter or calling an LLM API.

We need a senior engineer who can work across the full retrieval system—from data and indexing pipelines to embeddings, ranking, relevance, and low-latency serving—and take ambiguous product problems all the way to production.

You’ll join the specialised Data Search team and work closely with Data Core, Data Insights, product teams, customers, and company leadership. You’ll have real autonomy, but you won’t work in isolation.

If you want a feel for how we think about building software, check our Engineering Blog.

What you'll actually own

1. Make creator search meaningfully better.

You’ll improve how customers discover creators across 400M+ profiles and billions of media files. That includes retrieval, filtering, ranking, relevance, speed, and the product decisions that connect them.

2. Turn multimodal data into searchable intelligence.

You’ll build systems that generate and use embeddings from images, video, text, and audio at massive scale—then make those signals useful in a real customer-facing search experience.

3. Ship new search capabilities into production.

You’ll evaluate models and technologies pragmatically, understand tradeoffs around cost, latency, and quality, and move promising approaches from experiment to a reliable production system within weeks rather than quarters.

4. Own the system end to end.

You’ll help shape the problem, gather requirements, design the architecture, write the code, release it, measure the outcome, and improve it. Senior engineers here own results, not just implementation tasks.

What the day-to-day looks like

Here’s what a typical week might include:

  • Monday. A customer search is returning technically relevant but unhelpful results. You inspect the retrieval and ranking stages, identify where intent is being lost, and propose a measurable improvement.
  • Tuesday. Deep-focus time. You build a pipeline to generate multimodal embeddings across a large batch of creator content and test how the new representation affects retrieval quality and cost.
  • Wednesday. You work with Data Insights on a new in-house datapoint. Together, you agree on its definition, coverage, and data-quality requirements, then expose it in Search to give customers more ways to discover creators.
  • Thursday. You test a reranking model on a fixed set of real customer queries. You measure how much it improves relevance against the latency and inference cost it adds, then decide what's ready for production.
  • Friday. You review production metrics, investigate a relevance regression, and share what you learned with the team. The fix may be in the model, the data, the query logic, or the product itself—you follow the evidence.

We keep meetings purposeful and protect time for deep work. You’ll have a short standup, close collaboration when it helps, and plenty of space to design, build, optimise, and launch.

Requirements

What you've done before

  • Built large-scale data or backend products. You have solid experience working with systems where volume, latency, reliability, and cost all matter.
  • Shipped products from concept to production. You’ve owned scoping, architecture, implementation, release, measurement, and iteration—not just one layer of the solution.
  • Designed distributed systems. You can reason clearly about throughput, failure modes, data flow, scalability, and operational tradeoffs.
  • Built LLM-powered or agentic features in production. You understand the practical differences between models and can balance capability against latency and cost.
  • Worked autonomously on ambiguous problems. You know how to gather requirements, ask useful questions, and turn incomplete context into forward motion.
  • Communicated clearly across teams. You can explain technical tradeoffs to engineers and non-engineers, give direct feedback, and collaborate without creating unnecessary process.
  • Worked in a fast-moving product environment. You’re comfortable learning quickly, shipping incrementally, and changing direction when the evidence does.

Bonus points if you’ve worked with multimodal embeddings, vector databases, semantic search, ranking algorithms, model deployment, self-hosted models, or GPU infrastructure. Curiosity about the creator economy helps too, but we’ll get you up to speed.

Our stack

  • AWS and GCP, with Pulumi for infrastructure as code
  • Python, TypeScript, and Node.js
  • PySpark on AWS EMR
  • Airflow
  • Milvus Vector DB through Zilliz
  • Elasticsearch
  • LLM batch APIs
  • Apache Iceberg
  • SageMaker, DynamoDB, S3, Glue, Kinesis, Lambda, ECS, and Aurora
  • Slack, GitHub, Linear, Notion, and Cursor

The interview process

We move quickly and can complete the process in under a week:

  1. Intro chat
  2. Coding interview
  3. System design interview
  4. Team interview
  5. Culture and alignment conversation with our CEO, Avery Schrader

Benefits

What we offer

  • Fully remote in Europe 🏠 Work from wherever you do your best work, with some overlap with GMT+3.

  • Flexible hours ⏱ We care about outcomes, not when you log on.

  • Personal development support 🧠 Courses, books, and conferences are on us when they help you grow.
  • Real ownership 💡 Take difficult search problems from idea to production without layers of unnecessary process.
  • Regular offsites ✈️ We’re remote-first, but we make time to connect, collaborate, and have fun together in person.

Als Senior Account Executive führst du den gesamten Sales-Cycle – von der ersten Ansprache bis zum unterschriebenen Vertrag – eigenständig, mit klarem Kopf für Pipeline, Forecast und die Menschen auf der anderen Seite des Tisches.

PERSÖNLICHKEIT UND QUALIFIKATION

Was du mitbringst:

  • Erfahrung im Vertrieb erklärungsbedürftiger SaaS-Lösungen und ein sicheres Gespür für komplexe Sales-Zyklen

Weil Arbeit sich gut anfühlen soll, wenn großartige Dinge entstehen: Remote-Arbeit an erster Stelle, 30 Tage Urlaub, Family-First-Politik, keine Kleiderordnung, technische Wahlfreiheit. Unser Culture Code: Real Connections, Own Your Impact, Disruptive By Default, Serious Fun.

description: Your mission Servus und hallo bei uns in Sungrow! Manage and optimize enterprise network services across European locations, including routing, resilience, performance, capacity, and high-availability design. Take dedicated responsibility for Munich office connectivity, including switches, Wi-Fi, firewalls, VPNs, internet services, and meeting-room networks. Lead technical troubleshooting, incident response, root-cause analysis, and sustainable corrective actions for complex infrastructure issues. title: Senior Projektcontroller (m/w/d)
description: The Mission Du bist nicht einfach nur Controller. Du bist die Brücke zwischen Finance und Programm-Management. Während andere erst am Projektende auf die Marge schauen, weißt du schon in der Angebotsphase, ob sich ein Projekt rechnet – und steuerst es danach so präzise wie unsere Satelliten ihre Umlaufbahn. Während wir unsere Satellitenkonstellation ausbauen, wachsen Investitionen, Förderprojekte und Projektkomplexität. Du übersetzt Engineering- und Programmpläne in Forecasts, auf deren Basis das Management entscheiden kann – früh genug, um zu steuern. Für Förder- und Institutionsprojekte bist du Finance Owner. Du berichtest an den Director of Finance und arbeitest eng mit unserem Accounting Team, den Projektleiter:innen und Vertrieb zusammen. In dieser Rolle hast du echten Gestaltungsspielraum: Mit der Einführung von NetSuite Projects bietet sich dir die einmalige Chance, ein aussagekräftiges Projekt-Controlling mit aufzubauen – von der Projektstruktur über die Steuerungslogik bis zu einem Reporting, auf das sich Management und Projektleitung verlassen. What you’ll be doing Tech-Native (NetSuite Projects): Du führst NetSuite Projects (SuiteProjects) bei OroraTech ein – von der Projektstruktur (Projekttypen, Phasen, Budgets, Ressourcen) über Zeiterfassung und Kostenzuordnung bis zu Projekt-Dashboards. Du bist Key User und treibst die Automatisierung weiter. Angebotsphase: Du bist von Anfang an dabei. Du kalkulierst Angebote gemeinsam mit dem Vertrieb und der Projektleitung (Personal, Fremdleistungen, Hardware, Software, Risikozuschläge), bewertest Margen und Zahlungspläne und gibst eine fundierte Bid/No-Bid-Empfehlung. Für Förder- und Institutionsanträge (ESA, EU, national) baust du den Financial Case: Kosten- und Stundensatzmodelle, Kofinanzierungsstruktur sowie die Cash- und Reporting-Verpflichtungen, die jeder Antrag mit sich bringt. Profitabilitätssteuerung: Du verantwortest die wirtschaftliche Steuerung unseres Kundenprojekt-Portfolios. Du überwachst Budgets, Deckungsbeiträge und Cashflow je Projekt, erstellst Estimates at Completion (EAC) und leitest mit den Projektleiter:innen Gegenmaßnahmen ab, bevor Margen erodieren. CapEx-Projekte: Du verantwortest den Finanzplan unserer Investitionsprojekte – Satellitenbau, Payload-Entwicklung und Bodeninfrastruktur – von Budget und CapEx-Forecast über Cost-to-Complete und Aktivierung (Anlagen im Bau, aktivierte Eigenleistungen) bis zur Liquiditätswirkung. Abweichungsanalysen & Frühwarnung: Du führst monatliche Plan-Ist- und Forecast-Ist-Vergleiche auf Projektebene durch und bewertest Change Requests finanziell. Kostenüberschreitungen, Terminverzüge und Finanzierungslücken meldest du frühzeitig an das Management – immer mit einer konkreten Handlungsempfehlung. Förderprojekte: Nach Zuschlag steuerst du gemeinsam mit dem Grant Management die finanzielle Abwicklung: Nachverfolgung förderfähiger Kosten, Stundensatznachweise, Zuwendungserträge, Mittelabrufe, Verwendungsnachweise und Reporting-Pakete – mit einem Dokumentationspfad, der jeder Prüfung standhält. Abschluss & Umsatzrealisierung: Du lieferst dem Accounting die Projektdaten für Monats- und Jahresabschluss: Umsatzrealisierung (Meilenstein bzw. Leistungsfortschritt), unfertige Leistungen und Abgrenzungen nach HGB. Planung & Reporting : Deine Projektzahlen fließen in Unternehmensbudget, Forecast und Management-Reporting ein. Controlling-Framework: Du verantwortest das Projekt-Controlling-Framework – Kostenverteilungs- und Gemeinkostenregeln, Planungsmodelle, Reporting-Templates und das Tooling dahinter – als Fundament für Unternehmensplanung und FP&A. Point of Contact: Du bist die souveräne Ansprechperson für Projekt- und Programmleitung, Sales, Geschäftsführung und Accounting – und bei Förderprojekten auch für Projektträger und externe Prüfer. Relevant Skills Expertise: Abgeschlossenes Studium in BWL, Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen, Finance oder Controlling (oder vergleichbare Qualifikation) und mindestens sieben Jahre Erfahrung im Projektcontrolling, idealerweise im Tech-, Raumfahrt-, Engineering- oder Projektgeschäft. Projektwissen: Du beherrschst Angebotskalkulation, Deckungsbeitragsrechnung und projektbezogene Umsatzrealisierung. Du kennst geförderte oder öffentlich finanzierte Programme über den gesamten Zyklus – von Antragsbudget und Stundensatzmodell über Förderfähigkeitsregeln bis zu Mittelabrufen, Dokumentation und Compliance. IT-Affinität: Du hast tiefgehende Erfahrung mit modernen ERP-Systemen wie NetSuite oder SAP. Idealerweise hast du bereits ein Projektmodul eingeführt oder maßgeblich mitgestaltet. Kosten-, Stundensatz- und Gemeinkostenmodelle in Excel baust du im Schlaf. Mindset: Du arbeitest autark, liebst Gestaltungsfreiheit und übersetzt Engineering-Details in finanzielle Insights, mit denen auch Nicht-Finance-Kolleg:innen arbeiten können. Unbequeme Zahlen vermittelst du klar und konstruktiv. Sprachgefühl: Deutsch und Englisch sind für dich Standard. Nice to have: Erfahrung in projektbasierten, kapitalintensiven Umfeldern wie Raumfahrt, Luftfahrt, Verteidigung, Energie oder Infrastruktur. Direkte Erfahrung mit EU-, nationalen oder ESA-Förderprogrammen, deren Reporting- und Compliance-Vorgaben sowie mit Förder- oder externen Prüfungen. Erfahrung im CapEx-Controlling, mit Aktivierungsfragen oder langfristiger Projektbilanzierung. Erfahrung mit BI-Tools für Projekt-Dashboards. Our Benefits Flexibilität: Flexible Arbeitszeiten und Homeoffice-Option, auch aus dem EU-Ausland. Altersvorsorge: Betriebliche Altersvorsorge (bAV). Unfallversicherung: Weltweite Zusatzversicherung für Unfälle im Job und in der Freizeit, rund um die Uhr. Auslandsreisekrankenversicherung: Weltweiter Zusatzschutz auf Reisen, egal ob beruflich oder privat. Fitness: Vergünstigte EGYM-Wellpass-Mitgliedschaft. Mentale Gesundheit: Unterstützung für dein mentales Wohlbefinden über nilohealth. Mobilität: Kostenübernahme des DB Deutschland-Tickets. Lunch: Essenszuschuss über Hrmony. Bike-Leasing: Dein eigenes Dienstrad über JobRad. Office: Modernes Büro in der Neuen Balan mit Pool und Campus-Area. Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: AI Search Manager (m/w/d)
description: Du hast in einer führenden Agentur SEO gemacht. Jetzt machst du, was danach kommt. Du weißt, wie Rankings entstehen. Und du siehst, dass die Antwort immer öfter direkt in ChatGPT, Perplexity oder den AI Overviews steht. Für Marken zählt deshalb, ob sie dort als Quelle auftauchen. scaile - AI Visibility for Enterprise - ist der GEO Execution Layer. Wir recherchieren, schreiben, veröffentlichen und optimieren kontinuierlich den Content, mit dem Marken in ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Gemini und Perplexity gefunden und zitiert werden. Unterstützt von TUM Venture Labs und NCA VC, in Forschungspartnerschaft mit der TUM, sind wir bereits live mit Kunden wie UniCredit, Axel Springer, Beurer, Lyceum Technologies und 50 weiteren Unternehmen. Wir sind gerade in eine schnelle Wachstumsphase gestartet. Unsere Kunden zahlen für Ergebnisse, nicht für Artikel. Als AI Search Manager sorgst du dafür, dass diese Ergebnisse kommen. Du überträgst dein SEO-Handwerk auf eine neue Frage: Welche Quellen ziehen LLMs heran, und warum zitieren sie eine Marke? Die Antworten findest du in Daten und Experimenten. Die Tools dafür baust du dir mit Claude Code oder Codex selbst. Aufgaben Kundenprojekte: Du verantwortest die AI Visibility für ein eigenes Kundenportfolio, vom Kickoff-Workshop über Brand Kit und Content-Cluster bis zum laufenden Betrieb. Prompt Tracking: Du baust transaktionale Prompt-Sets auf und misst Zitationen, Brand Mentions, Sentiment und Platzierung, auch im Vergleich zum Wettbewerb. Strategie: Du analysierst, welche Quellen LLMs zitieren und warum. Daraus leitest du Content-Cluster, Briefings und Prioritäten für unsere Content Engine ab. Technische Basis: Du prüfst Crawler-Zugriff (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot und Co.), Rendering und strukturierte Daten und begleitest die Anbindung ans CMS oder CDN. Automatisierung: Mit Claude Code oder Codex baust du dir Audits, Datenabzüge, Auswertungen und kleine interne Tools selbst. Reporting: Du zeigst Kunden im wöchentlichen Termin, was sich bewegt, von Klicks und CTR bis zu Zitationen in AI Search, und leitest klare nächste Schritte ab. Experimente: Du testest, was in AI Search funktioniert, hältst Inhalte aktuell und bringst Learnings mit Product und Engineering ins Produkt. Dein Erfolg ist messbar: wie viel mehr Conversion wurde durch die Sichtbarkeit in der KI Suche erzielt. Qualifikation 1-2 Jahre Berufserfahrung als SEO Manager in einer führenden SEO- oder Digitalagentur. Du hast eigene Kundenprojekte verantwortet und kennst technisches SEO und Content-SEO aus der Praxis. Du bist vertraut mit Claude Code oder Codex und hast damit schon Skripte, Automatisierungen oder kleine Tools gebaut. Du willst verstehen, wie LLMs Quellen auswählen, und testest das lieber selbst, als darüber zu lesen. Google Search Console, Sistrix oder Ahrefs und Screaming Frog sind für dich Routine. Du kommunizierst klar und trittst vor Enterprise-Kunden sicher auf. Low ego, high ownership - dir ist wichtiger, dass es richtig ist, als recht zu haben. Deutsch auf C2-Niveau und sehr gutes Englisch, in Wort und Schrift. Gültige Arbeitserlaubnis für Deutschland. Nice to have: Python- oder SQL-Grundlagen, erste Berührung mit AEO/GEO oder Prompt Tracking. Benefits Wettbewerbsfähiges Gehalt. Echte Ownership: deine Kunden, deine Ergebnisse. Direkter Draht zu den Gründern, flache Hierarchien, kurze Wege. Ein Feld, das gerade entsteht: AI Search. Du lernst es nicht aus Blogposts, du prägst mit, wie es gemacht wird. Nah an der Forschung durch unsere Partnerschaft mit der TUM. Regelmäßige Teamevents Dinner ab 20:00 Urbansportsclub Drinks, Snacks und Kaffe Uber nach 22:00 Büro mitten in München/Hamburg, Team von 11+ Leuten. You'll operate at the intersection of individual client engagements - spanning DAX corporations to leading “Mittelstand” businesses - and appliedAI's broader design practice, working closely with adjacent teams such as Change & Enablement and Trustworthy AI to turn deep UX expertise into real-world impact.
Your tasks will include:

  • Own the user experience strategy across our most demanding client AI engagements - from discovery and early concept through validated, handover-ready designs that clients' engineering teams can build with confidence
  • Shape UX and CX strategy across engagements - framing the actual problem before a single screen is designed, running discovery and moderated research sessions with operators, planners, and engineers, so design decisions rest on evidence rather than opinion
  • Define the interaction patterns agentic systems need - human-in-the-loop approval, latency and status communication, source attribution, uncertainty and error states, and safe defaults for irreversible actions
  • Set the standard for how we design and modernize complex, operationally critical systems - dense data, high stakes, long-lived workflows, and users who cannot afford to guess what the system just did
  • Drive adoption of shared design systems and component libraries across engagements - specifications and patterns that make the next project faster, not a slide deck about consistency
  • Establish DesignOps and design governance across our project portfolio - methodologies, review rituals, and quality bars that scale experience maturity across multi-stakeholder programs, with accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA / EN 301 549) as a non-negotiable design requirement validated in close partnership with engineering
  • Own and evolve appliedAI's experience and design standards across the whole professional services organization, and raise the craft bar through review, critique, and mentoring


Your profile

  • Extensive experience, typically 10+ years, in experience design and design leadership, including leading or growing a multidisciplinary UX/design practice, with deep command of the end-to-end product design process from research through detailed interaction and visual design
  • Comfortable working at the boundary with engineering and being able to translate a design system into implementation-ready specifications and hold a high bar in review, without needing to ship production code yourself
  • A track record designing for complex, data-dense, operationally critical enterprise systems like industrial, infrastructure, control-room or comparable environments, delivered inside multi-stakeholder programs
  • Proven experience establishing DesignOps, governance models, and design methodologies that raise experience maturity beyond your own projects with designing systems, quality gates, and process frameworks that other teams actually adopt
  • Experience designing for AI or data-heavy products is a strong plus - non-deterministic output, latency, trust, and explainability change the design problem fundamentally
  • A trusted strategic advisor in ambiguous, client-facing settings, facilitating workshops, navigating conflicting stakeholder interests, and delivering difficult messages diplomatically, with the credibility to operate from C-suite conversations down to the operators who use the system
  • Fluent in English, German a strong plus as part of our client work happens in German


What we offer

  • A highly qualified and motivated team of ~90 people is on a journey to change the rapidly evolving European AI Landscape
  • Experience the best of both worlds with our hybrid work model: You can choose to work from our vibrant offices - either at the IPAI in Heilbronn or the House of Communication in Munich - while also enjoying the flexibility to work remotely a few days each week
  • Opportunity to shape a variety of projects and the development of new, original content based on the latest developments in AI and its adoption in businesses
  • An atmosphere that encourages to think and experiment in new ways with software, hardware, and processes
  • A highly visible initiative that helps you build a large and high-level network of start-ups, partners, and tech companies
  • A flexible development budget that’s yours to shape - invest it in training, certifications, conferences, or new challenges, however you want to grow
  • Sports membership with Wellpass to access thousands of sports facilities all over Germany (and beyond), as well as online courses
  • JobRad: Lease a bike for a cheaper rate via JobRad and we cover the bike insurance on top

description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong>Our Why At Dotmatics&nbsp;</strong></p> <p>At Dotmatics, a Siemens company,&nbsp; we believe science, data, and decision-making must be deeply intertwined for innovation to thrive. description: About Notabene Notabene is building infrastructure that's transforming how money moves in the digital economy. We're evolving beyond our compliance foundations to enable the next generation of digital financial services between regulated institutions with unprecedented efficiency. With nearly 50 employees across 14 countries and having recently closed our Series B round last November with support from leading investors including Y Combinator, DRW, F-Prime, Jump Capital, Castle Island, and Green Visor Capital, we're looking for people like you to help shape the future rails of the crypto industry. Location: US-based, Remote East Coast The impact you will have Notabene is planning on going through its first external financial statement audit, covering the fiscal years ending January 2026 and January 2027. You will own that process. You will also own the close, the books, and the accounting policy for a two-entity, multi-currency business whose revenue includes subscription fees, usage-based transaction billing, and a payments network take rate that has no clean accounting precedent anywhere. The accounting function is already substantially built. Close runs, the books are in order, and readiness work for the audit is well underway. What we need is someone to own it, finish it, and take it through the audit, while raising the standard on policy and documentation as the business gets more complex. You will be the most senior accounting voice in the company, reporting to the VP of Finance, with one direct report and a set of external providers. You will not have a large team before late 2027, and that is deliberate. Capacity here comes from better systems and better automation, and you will be the one deciding what those look like. Within a year you are successful if Notabene has a clean audit opinion on both fiscal years, with no material weaknesses and no second cycle on auditor requests The close hits its calendar consistently, starting with the revenue close landing on time Revenue recognition is documented in a written memo that stands up in fieldwork, rather than living only in the billing system configuration Multi-entity consolidation and FX translation run cleanly enough to survive audit scrutiny, with intercompany and CTA tied and supported Payroll allocation across departments and software development capitalization are written policy applied consistently, not judgment applied after the fact Key accounting controls are documented, operating, and evidenced At least two accounting processes that are manual today run without a person in the loop, and still hold up under audit What you will be doing Audit. Run the readiness assessment, build the remediation plan, contribute the technical view on which firm we engage, and then own the auditor relationship day to day. Close and reporting. Own the monthly, quarterly, and annual close across Notabene Inc. and Notabene GmbH. Produce GAAP financial statements, consolidations, intercompany eliminations, and FX translation under ASC 830. Technical accounting. Write the positions and the memos. ASC 606 across three revenue models, ASC 350-40 for internal-use software capitalization, ASC 718 for stock compensation expense, and whatever emerges as stablecoin payment revenue matures. Revenue and billing systems. Own Tabs as the billing and revenue system of record, including contract configuration, usage data integrity, and the bridge from Tabs to the general ledger. Cost accounting. Build the payroll allocation method for people whose work splits across functions, and the capitalization policy for development work, so departmental margin reflects where effort actually goes. Controls. Design and implement controls over revenue, cash, procure to pay, and payroll. Not SOX. Controls that operate, are evidenced, and can be walked by an auditor. Automation. Evaluate the accounting stack and the processes running on it with a bias toward automation, including agentic tooling where work is rule-bound and high volume. Categorization, reconciliation matching, usage validation, and collections follow-up are the obvious places to start. Accounting operations. Own AR and collections with your direct report, plus AP and payroll accounting. Employee onboarding and HRIS administration sit with People, not with you. Tax. Own US tax compliance in coordination with our external advisers, including the income tax provision and sales tax. Coordinate Swiss compliance with our local accountants. External providers. raw.description:
About Notabene

Notabene is building infrastructure that's transforming how money moves in the digital economy. We're evolving beyond our compliance foundations to enable the next generation of digital financial services between regulated institutions with unprecedented efficiency. With nearly 50 employees across 14 countries and having recently closed our Series B round last November with support from leading investors including Y Combinator, DRW, F-Prime, Jump Capital, Castle Island, and Green Visor Capital, we're looking for people like you to help shape the future rails of the crypto industry.

Location:

US-based, Remote East Coast

The impact you will have

Notabene is planning on going through its first external financial statement audit, covering the fiscal years ending January 2026 and January 2027. You will own that process. You will also own the close, the books, and the accounting policy for a two-entity, multi-currency business whose revenue includes subscription fees, usage-based transaction billing, and a payments network take rate that has no clean accounting precedent anywhere.

The accounting function is already substantially built. Close runs, the books are in order, and readiness work for the audit is well underway. What we need is someone to own it, finish it, and take it through the audit, while raising the standard on policy and documentation as the business gets more complex. You will be the most senior accounting voice in the company, reporting to the VP of Finance, with one direct report and a set of external providers. You will not have a large team before late 2027, and that is deliberate. Capacity here comes from better systems and better automation, and you will be the one deciding what those look like.

Within a year you are successful if

  • Notabene has a clean audit opinion on both fiscal years, with no material weaknesses and no second cycle on auditor requests

  • The close hits its calendar consistently, starting with the revenue close landing on time

  • Revenue recognition is documented in a written memo that stands up in fieldwork, rather than living only in the billing system configuration

  • Multi-entity consolidation and FX translation run cleanly enough to survive audit scrutiny, with intercompany and CTA tied and supported

  • Payroll allocation across departments and software development capitalization are written policy applied consistently, not judgment applied after the fact

  • Key accounting controls are documented, operating, and evidenced

  • At least two accounting processes that are manual today run without a person in the loop, and still hold up under audit

What you will be doing

Audit. Run the readiness assessment, build the remediation plan, contribute the technical view on which firm we engage, and then own the auditor relationship day to day.

Close and reporting. Own the monthly, quarterly, and annual close across Notabene Inc. and Notabene GmbH. Produce GAAP financial statements, consolidations, intercompany eliminations, and FX translation under ASC 830.

Technical accounting. Write the positions and the memos. ASC 606 across three revenue models, ASC 350-40 for internal-use software capitalization, ASC 718 for stock compensation expense, and whatever emerges as stablecoin payment revenue matures.

Revenue and billing systems. Own Tabs as the billing and revenue system of record, including contract configuration, usage data integrity, and the bridge from Tabs to the general ledger.

Cost accounting. Build the payroll allocation method for people whose work splits across functions, and the capitalization policy for development work, so departmental margin reflects where effort actually goes.

Controls. Design and implement controls over revenue, cash, procure to pay, and payroll. Not SOX. Controls that operate, are evidenced, and can be walked by an auditor.

Automation. Evaluate the accounting stack and the processes running on it with a bias toward automation, including agentic tooling where work is rule-bound and high volume. Categorization, reconciliation matching, usage validation, and collections follow-up are the obvious places to start.

Accounting operations. Own AR and collections with your direct report, plus AP and payroll accounting. Employee onboarding and HRIS administration sit with People, not with you.

Tax. Own US tax compliance in coordination with our external advisers, including the income tax provision and sales tax. Coordinate Swiss compliance with our local accountants.

External providers. We produce revenue in-house, our Swiss accountants produce their piece, and our outsourced firm assembles the close. You will own the checklist, the policies, and the reconciliations, so providers execute against a Notabene-owned close rather than holding it themselves.

What you bring

  • Experience as a Controller, Assistant Controller, or Senior Accounting Manager at a venture-backed company, with a track record of raising the standard on process rather than just running what exists

  • You have taken a company through a first external audit and can describe specifically what broke and what you did about it

  • Month-end close ownership across two or more legal entities in different currencies

  • Deep, hands-on ASC 606, applied to at least one revenue model without clean precedent, and defended to an auditor

  • You operate in the detail. You build the calendar, do the reconciliations, and touch the ledger

  • Experience developing a small team or a single direct report

Nice to have

  • Active CPA license

  • Usage-based or consumption billing experience, particularly Tabs, Metronome, Maxio, or similar

  • Public accounting background, especially audit

  • Software development capitalization under ASC 350-40, including the time capture that makes it auditable

  • Experience replacing manual accounting work with automation, and a clear view on what should stay manual

  • Swiss entity experience, including CHF functional currency and Swiss statutory or VAT exposure

  • Digital assets, payments, or regulated financial services exposure

Benefits

Flexible Remote Work: Work from anywhere! $1000 WFH Stipend: Use within your first year of employment. MacBook Pro: Procured by you and your manager to find a model that meets your needs. Unlimited PTO: We trust you to take as much holiday as you need. Country-Specific Benefits: Statutory offerings and contributions, managed via our employer-of-record.

Apply Today!

If you strongly believe this role is for you, please apply. Notabene considers a broad array of candidates, including those without blockchain experience. description: <div class="content-intro"><p><span style="font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif;">SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge.&nbsp;</span><span style="font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif;">Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. </span><span style="font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif;">All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.</span></p></div><h3 data-pm-slice="1 1 []"><span style="font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif;">ABOUT THE ROLE:</span></h3> <p>We are seeking an experienced Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) Engineer focused on European Union and United Kingdom information security and financial services regulation to help scale compliance for SpaceXAI and xMoney. As we expand deeper into regulated EU/UK markets, maintaining a robust, transparent, and technically sound information security GRC program is critical. You will architect the systems and processes that automate trust — a pragmatic operator who understands that GRC exists to enable the business, balancing rigorous standards with the velocity of a high-growth company. The ideal candidate brings hands-on experience with frameworks such as DORA, the EU AI Act, NIS2, and related EU/UK information security and operational resilience obligations, plus GRC engineering skills: Compliance-as-Code, continuous evidence collection, and deep partnership with engineering so controls are designed into the platform rather than bolted on after the fact.</p> <p><em>This role may also include additional tasks and responsibilities as needed to support the team and evolving business priorities. This position may require occasional travel.</em></p> <h3><span style="font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif;">RESPONSIBILITIES:</span></h3> <ul> <li>Own and evolve EU/UK financial services and digital operational resilience posture across DORA (including ICT risk management, incident reporting, resilience testing, and third-party ICT provider oversight), and complementary expectations from EBA/ESMA/EIOPA guidance, PSD2/PSR where applicable, and UK PRA/FCA operational resilience requirements supporting xMoney.</li> <li>Build and maintain Compliance-as-Code capabilities — policy-as-code, automated control validation, continuous evidence collection, and monitoring integrated into CI/CD — so audit and supervisory readiness scales with the business rather than depending on manual, point-in-time checks.</li> <li>Operate and extend GRC platforms (e.g., Vanta) as the backbone for control mapping, evidence management, and continuous compliance; integrate with cloud, identity, logging, and engineering systems to reduce administrative bottlenecks.</li> <li>Partner with Architects and Engineering Leads to bake EU/UK information security and regulatory requirements into design early; translate complex obligations into concrete technical implementations and auditor- or supervisor-ready narratives without slowing development.</li> <li>Design, implement, and validate technical information security controls relevant to regulated EU/UK environments (access control, logging and monitoring, encryption, change management, vulnerability management, ICT third-party oversight, and secure SDLC) — not just document them.</li> <li>Operate the cybersecurity and compliance risk register — identify, quantify, and track risks, distinguishing theoretical gaps from meaningful business and regulatory risk under EU/UK supervisory expectations.</li> <li>Lead information security risk assessments and compliance reviews for new products, features, vendors, and architectural changes that affect the EU/UK regulated attack surface, including ICT third-party / critical provider diligence aligned to DORA.</li> <li>Liaise with the Data Privacy team on security-relevant intersections (e.g., security measures supporting confidentiality and integrity.</li> <li>Own and cultivate relationships with external auditors, assessors, and (where applicable) supervisory contacts on information security topics; serve as the bridge between external parties and internal teams so requests are reasonable, clear, and relevant to our stack.</li> <li>Develop, maintain, and continuously improve information security policies, standards, and procedures aligned to DORA, the EU AI Act, NIS2 where in scope, and complementary frameworks (e.g., ISO 27001, SOC 2) where they overlap.</li> <li>Champion pragmatic governance — prioritize issues that represent real security or business risk over checkbox compliance.</li> </ul> <h3><span style="font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif;">BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</span></h3> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in computer science, Information Security, Cybersecurity, or in an engineering/STEM field.</li> <li>8+ years of experience in GRC, information security compliance, or technology audit roles in fintech, banking, payments, or other heavily regulated environments with EU and/or UK exposure.</li> <li>Hands-on experience implementing or operating controls against several of the following: DORA, the EU AI Act, NIS2, PSD2/PSR, or UK PRA/FCA operational resilience expectations — not only reading the requirements.</li> <li>Familiar with data privacy regulations applicable to the EU/UK region (e.g., EU GDPR, UK GDPR, UK Data Protection Act 2018) sufficient to liaise with Privacy counterparts.</li> <li>Experience with Compliance-as-Code practices and GRC automation tooling (e.g., Vanta, or similar), with a bias toward continuous monitoring and reducing manual evidence collection.</li> <li>Technical fluency sufficient to speak the language of engineering, On-premises, hybrid, or cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure), and security architecture, and to anticipate how design decisions impact information security risk and compliance.</li> </ul> <h3><span style="font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif;">PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</span></h3> <ul> <li>10+ years of information security compliance, GRC engineering, or technology audit-related experience in fintech or financial services with a primary EU/UK focus.</li> <li>Hands-on experience implementing technical controls (e.g., IAM, logging and monitoring, encryption, network segmentation, infrastructure hardening) and integrating compliance checks into CI/CD pipelines.</li> <li>Experience supporting ISO 27001 and/or SOC 2 programs alongside EU/UK regulatory obligations.</li> <li>Familiar with GDPR concepts that commonly intersect with information security (e.g., security of processing, breach notification timelines, encryption/pseudonymization as security measures) when collaborating with DPO/Legal/Privacy functions.</li> <li>Familiarity with DORA ICT third-party risk, register of information, threat-led penetration testing (TLPT) concepts, and major ICT-related incident reporting expectations.</li> <li>Experience with AI governance under the EU AI Act or related national guidance, especially security controls for AI features in regulated financial products.</li> <li>Familiar with related regional regimes that may touch information security scope (e.g., ePrivacy, Digital Services Act touchpoints, MiCA where relevant to product scope, or FCA Consumer Duty technology implications).</li> <li>Experience enabling enterprise sales through trust centers, vendor questionnaires, and customer security reviews for EU/UK buyers.</li> <li>Proven ability to operate a risk register and apply judgment in gray areas — focusing on outcomes over optics.</li> <li>Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and project management skills, with the ability to take compliance programs from conception to assessment-ready launch.</li> <li>Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills — able to explain information security and regulatory requirements to engineers, legal, privacy, sales, and executives in plain language.</li> <li>Certifications such as CISSP, CISA, CISM, CRISC, ISO 27001 Lead Implementer/Auditor, or similar preferred; are a plus for liaison fluency, not a substitute for security depth.</li> <li>Prior experience working with or within EU/UK-regulated financial institutions, EMI/PI environments, or supervised fintechs is a plus.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><em>SpaceXAI is an equal opportunity employer. description: What We Do Rillet serves accounting and finance teams, the financial brains of their companies. Our job is to help them run the numbers with impossible speed, accuracy, and insight. Rillet is the Agentic ERP built for modern finance teams. We help companies automate the most critical parts of finance, from closing the books and recognizing revenue to consolidating entities and reporting to investors. More than 600 companies run on Rillet, including Mercor, Scribe, and Function Health, and we partner with leading accounting firms including EY and KPMG. We’re building in one of the largest software markets in the world, with the momentum to match. Rillet has raised more than $200M, is valued at $1B, and is backed by Sequoia, a16z, ICONIQ, Bain Capital Ventures, Oak HC/FT, and other leading investors. We’re using that backing to build the financial infrastructure for the next generation of companies and help every business run its numbers at the speed of AI. Who We Are Rillet’s pace is not for everyone. Intelligence is table stakes. To succeed here, you need extreme speed, agency, and flexibility. The people who thrive at Rillet do not wait for assignments. They internalize the mission, design a strategy, and bring back results that are better, faster, and more creative than a manager could have asked for. Our work revolves around our customers. The people who succeed here are energized by delivering what matters most, even when it was not part of the original plan. Rillet is built on deep accounting expertise, and it takes people from many disciplines to build a category-defining company. You do not need to be an accountant to thrive here. You do need to care deeply about the problems we solve and the impact our customers can create. Together, we combine the precision of accounting with the speed, creativity, and ambition of AI-native software to power the financial core of the world’s fastest-growing companies while redefining what finance teams should expect from their software. Who We Need We’re looking for an accountant who wants to be a builder—whether you’ve already moved into a client-facing/solutions role or you’re a current accountant ready to apply your craft with modern tools. Having previous professional accounting or audit experience will allow the candidate to build immediate trust with our customers. You’ll own the long-term relationship with our customers after sales and implementation, partnering with CFOs, Controllers, and Accounting Managers to deliver scalable, automated solutions on Rillet’s AI platform. If you enjoy solving complex accounting problems, client interaction, system configuration, and measurable impact—but don’t have a traditional “Customer Success” background—this role is for you. What You'll Do Own customer relationships and outcomes: Build deep relationships across your customer portfolio, run success plans, and hold recurring meetings to maximize value attainment of Rillet. Deliver unique AI-driven accounting solutions: Translate complex accounting challenges into automated workflows powered by Rillet’s AI platform. Apply accounting expertise: Bridge the gap between technical product capabilities and customer accounting needs, ensuring solutions meet real-world requirements. Drive platform adoption and expansion: Lead trainings to ensure customers are continuously enabled on the platform, advise on process optimization and month-end close efficiency. Cross-functional collaboration: Provide front-line customer feedback to founders and Product in close to real-time, triage support issues with Engineering, and ensure smooth account handoff with Implementation. Become a Product Expert: Develop deep product expertise in Rillet’s AI-native platform, staying up-to-date on the latest features and functionality. Represent Rillet: You’ll be the face of the company and will apply high customer empathy and structured problem-solving to ensure every customer interaction is delightful. Who We're Looking For 3+ years of hands-on accounting experience (public audit/assurance or industry GL/Close, Revenue, AP, or Consolidations). Understanding of UK GAAP and the end-to-end close process — even better if you have exposure to IFRS and technical accounting concepts like IFRS 15 / revenue recognition. Proven ability to translate accounting requirements into system configurations and automated workflows. Experience with ERPs (e.g., NetSuite, Intacct) and comfort picking up new finance tools. Bias to action, ownership mindset, and high attention to detail in a fast-moving environment. CPA (active or inactive); prior client-facing/consulting or implementation experience (not required). Life at Rillet Grow with us. Take meaningful ownership, expand your scope, and make an impact as Rillet scales. Competitive pay and meaningful equity. Be rewarded for the value you help create. Benefits that support you. We offer competitive benefits designed to support your health, wellbeing, time away from work, family, and long-term financial goals. Better together. We value collaboration, connection, and spending meaningful time together as a team. We regularly create opportunities to connect through team meals, events, and company gatherings.
